300	/// A `during` slot that is actually running: `period` above zero, and a
301	/// duration to measure a drift against.
302	fn live_during(motion: &Motion, duration: f64) -> Option<(MotionDuring, f64, f64)> {
303	    let slot = motion.during?;
304	    let period = slot.period as f64;
305	    if period <= 0.0 || !period.is_finite() {
306	        return None;
307	    }
308	    // A drift divides by the clip's duration; every other kind ignores it.
309	    if matches!(slot.kind, DuringMotion::Drift) && duration <= 0.0 {
310	        return None;
311	    }
312	    let amount = if slot.amount.is_finite() {
313	        slot.amount.clamp(0.0, 1.0)
314	    } else {
315	        0.0
316	    };
317	    Some((slot, amount, period))
318	}

320	/// `video` with its five placed fields moved by whatever `video.motion`
321	/// asks for at `clip_t`. Every other field is the input's.
322	///
323	/// `size` is the source's pixel size (`Project::source_size`), `None` for
324	/// text; `container` is the canvas the clip is placed in — the project's,
325	/// or the frozen canvas of the nest it lives inside. See the module doc.
326	pub(crate) fn apply(
327	    video: &VideoProps,
328	    clip_t: Ticks,
329	    duration: Ticks,
330	    size: Option<(f64, f64)>,
331	    container: (f64, f64),
332	) -> VideoProps {
333	    let Some(motion) = video.motion else {
334	        return video.clone();
335	    };
336	    let t = clip_t as f64;
337	    let d = duration as f64;
338	    let (arrive, leave) = tent(&motion, d);
339	
340	    let arrival_term = motion.r#in.filter(|_| arrive > 0.0 && t < arrive).map(|e| {
341	        let u = t / arrive;
342	        arrival(
343	            e.kind,
344	            crate::actions::ease(crate::model::Curve::EaseOut, u),
345	            u,
346	        )
347	    });
348	    let departure_term = motion
349	        .out
350	        .filter(|_| leave > 0.0 && t >= d - leave)
351	        .map(|e| {
352	            let v = 1.0 - (d - t) / leave;
353	            departure(
354	                e.kind,
355	                crate::actions::ease(crate::model::Curve::EaseIn, v),
356	                v,
357	            )
358	        });
359	    let during_term = live_during(&motion, d).map(|(slot, amount, period)| {
360	        during(slot.kind, amount, t, period, d, container.0, container.1)
361	    });
362	
363	    // Nothing running: the clip is exactly where it is placed, and saying so
364	    // by cloning rather than by computing an identity is what makes the
365	    // frame byte-identical to a clip with no motion (module doc).
366	    if arrival_term.is_none() && departure_term.is_none() && during_term.is_none() {
367	        return video.clone();
368	    }
369	
370	    let terms = [&arrival_term, &departure_term, &during_term];
371	    let mut factor = 1.0_f64;
372	    let mut phi = 0.0_f64;
373	    let mut opacity_factor = 1.0_f64;
374	    let mut delta = (0.0_f64, 0.0_f64);
375	    for term in terms.iter().filter_map(|t| t.as_ref()) {
376	        factor *= term.f;
377	        phi += term.phi;
378	        delta.0 += term.delta.0;
379	        delta.1 += term.delta.1;
380	    }
381	    // Opacity is the two EDGES only — a during never fades, so folding the
382	    // third term in would be a factor of 1 that could still round.
383	    for term in [&arrival_term, &departure_term]
384	        .iter()
385	        .filter_map(|t| t.as_ref())
386	    {
387	        opacity_factor *= term.o;
388	    }
389	    let phi = if phi.is_finite() {
390	        // `rem_euclid` alone cannot keep the reduction's promise: it is
391	        // `let r = self % rhs; if r < 0.0 { r + rhs.abs() } else { r }`, and
392	        // for a φ of −2e-14 that addition ROUNDS UP to exactly 360.0 — the
393	        // one value the reduction exists to prevent. An arrival `spin` one
394	        // tick from its end produces exactly that φ.
395	        let reduced = phi.rem_euclid(360.0);
396	        // And a double merely NEAR 360 is no better than 360 itself, because
397	        // `Compositor.swift`'s `partnerBox` guard tests `rotation == 0`
398	        // EXACTLY, on the recipe's f64 (`RecipeLayer.rotation` is a `Double`):
399	        // a layer that is unrotated to the eye has to publish an exact zero,
400	        // and the same arrival one tick earlier reaches 359.99999999999994,
401	        // which fails that guard exactly as 360.0 does. So a BAND under a
402	        // whole turn is published as no turn. The band is CHOSEN, not read off
403	        // a consumer: "rounds to 360 as an f32 of DEGREES", a convenient
404	        // conservative width of 2⁻¹⁶ of a degree (1.5259e-5°). No f32 of
405	        // degrees exists anywhere: the one f32 is the Metal uniform,
406	        // `Float(rotation · π/180)`, RADIANS, which conflates only doubles
407	        // within 3.64e-6° of a turn (a band 4.2× narrower) and which the guard
408	        // never sees. What justifies the width is the PICTURE: 1.5259e-5°
409	        // moves the corner of a 4K frame (√(1920² + 1080²) = 2202.9 px from
410	        // its centre) by at most 5.87e-4 px. What the rule actually moves is
411	        // 1.998e-14° one tick from an arrival's end and 1.0e-5° at the
412	        // `during` `core/tests/motion_edges.rs` pins.
413	        if reduced as f32 >= 360.0 {
414	            0.0
415	        } else {
416	            reduced
417	        }
418	    } else {
419	        0.0
420	    };
421	
422	    let base_scale = if video.scale.is_finite() {
423	        video.scale
424	    } else {
425	        1.0
426	    };
427	    let base_rotation = if video.rotation.is_finite() {
428	        video.rotation
429	    } else {
430	        0.0
431	    };
432	    let drawn_scale = (base_scale * factor).clamp(SCALE_MIN, SCALE_MAX);
433	    let drawn_rotation = base_rotation + phi;
434	
435	    // The cropped rect's centre in source pixels (★'s `c`), and the visible
436	    // size the slide box is measured from. Text has neither, so it takes the
437	    // half-canvas rule the module doc records as a limit.
438	    let crop = video.crop;
439	    let (centre, half_x, half_y) = match size {
440	        Some((sw, sh)) => {
441	            let visible_w = (sw - crop.l - crop.r).max(0.0);
442	            let visible_h = (sh - crop.t - crop.b).max(0.0);
443	            let k = drawn_rotation.to_radians().cos().abs();
444	            let n = drawn_rotation.to_radians().sin().abs();
445	            (
446	                ((crop.l - crop.r) / 2.0, (crop.t - crop.b) / 2.0),
447	                drawn_scale * (visible_w * k + visible_h * n) / 2.0,
448	                drawn_scale * (visible_w * n + visible_h * k) / 2.0,
449	            )
450	        }
451	        None => ((0.0, 0.0), container.0 / 2.0, container.1 / 2.0),
452	    };
453	
454	    // The BASE visible centre — where the pivot compensation below holds the
455	    // layer whatever the other slots do to scale and rotation.
456	    let base_pivot = rotate(centre.0 * base_scale, centre.1 * base_scale, base_rotation);
457	    let p = (video.x + base_pivot.0, video.y + base_pivot.1);
458	    let side = |side: Side| match side {
459	        Side::Right => (container.0 / 2.0 + half_x - p.0, 0.0),
460	        Side::Left => (-(container.0 / 2.0 + half_x) - p.0, 0.0),
461	        Side::Bottom => (0.0, container.1 / 2.0 + half_y - p.1),
462	        Side::Top => (0.0, -(container.1 / 2.0 + half_y) - p.1),
463	    };
464	    for term in terms.iter().filter_map(|t| t.as_ref()) {
465	        if let Some((edge, fraction)) = term.slide {
466	            let (sx, sy) = side(edge);
467	            delta.0 += fraction * sx;
468	            delta.1 += fraction * sy;
469	        }
470	    }
471	
472	    let drawn_pivot = rotate(
473	        centre.0 * drawn_scale,
474	        centre.1 * drawn_scale,
475	        drawn_rotation,
476	    );
477	    let x = video.x + base_pivot.0 - drawn_pivot.0 + delta.0;
478	    let y = video.y + base_pivot.1 - drawn_pivot.1 + delta.1;
479	    let opacity = video.opacity * opacity_factor;
480	
481	    // A non-finite result leaves that field AS EVALUATED rather than
482	    // poisoning the frame: no NaN reaches the recipe.
483	    let keep = |moved: f64, evaluated: f64| if moved.is_finite() { moved } else { evaluated };
484	    VideoProps {
485	        x: keep(x, video.x),
486	        y: keep(y, video.y),
487	        scale: keep(drawn_scale, video.scale),
488	        rotation: keep(drawn_rotation, video.rotation),
489	        opacity: keep(opacity.clamp(0.0, 1.0), video.opacity),
490	        ..video.clone()
491	    }
492	}
493	        let existing = target
494	            .actions
495	            .iter()
496	            .find(|a| a.id == action)
497	            .ok_or_else(|| format!("no action with id {action} on clip {clip}"))?;
498	        if !patch.is_object() {
499	            return Err(format!(
500	                "action end patch must be a json object, not {}",
501	                describe(patch)
502	            ));
503	        }
504	        if let Some(schema) = schema {
505	            check_schema(schema)?;
506	        }
507	        // Present at all — a `null` included, since writing `motion: null`
508	        // into an end patch is still asking an action to decide a preset.
509	        for (group, key) in [
510	            ("video", "motion"),
511	            ("video", "hide_silent"),
512	            ("text", "words"),
513	        ] {
514	            if patch.get(group).and_then(|body| body.get(key)).is_some() {
515	                not_a_target(group, key)?;
516	            }
517	        }
518	        check_cutout_end(patch)?;
519	        check_end_patch(patch)?;
520	        let graphic = match patch.get("graphic") {
521	            Some(body) => Some(read_graphic_end(target, body, schema)?),

## Motion presets

A motion preset says what a clip **does** rather than where it is. Each clip has three slots: an **In** (an entrance at its start), an **Out** (an exit at its end) and a **During** (a movement for its whole length). A preset is tied to the clip's ends, so it moves with a trim. It works on any clip that draws a picture: video, still images, text, shapes, graphics and nests.

Motion is applied on top of the clip's own placement and any actions, and it is never animated by an action. A preset works relative to the clip: its scale and opacity multiply the clip's own, and its rotation and offset add to them. Zoom and Spin turn about the clip's visible centre, after any crop. The inspector fields (and `get_project`) show the clip's own, un-moved values, even though the preview and export show it moving.

### Set a preset

Use the **Motion presets** section at the end of the Clip sub-tab, or **Clip ▸ Motion ▸ In**, **Out** or **During**. Each submenu lists the kinds, then **None** to clear the slot. A checkmark shows the kind every selected clip shares.

The section's rows:

| Row | What it does | Range | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| In | The entrance kind, or None | None and nine kinds | None |
| In Duration | How long the entrance takes (disabled with None) | 0.1–10 s (quick picks 0.25, 0.5, 1) | 0.5 s |
| Out | The exit kind, or None | None and nine kinds | None |
| Out Duration | How long the exit takes (disabled with None) | 0.1–10 s (quick picks 0.25, 0.5, 1) | 0.5 s |
| During | The continuous movement, or None | None and five kinds | None |
| Amount | How strong the During movement is (disabled with None) | 0–100% (quick picks 25, 50, 75, 100) | 50% |
| Period | How long one cycle takes (disabled with None and for Drift) | 0.1–10 s (quick picks 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2) | 1 s |
| Preview | Sets the in/out range to the clip, turns Loop on and plays it | | |

Changing a slot's kind keeps the duration, amount and period it already had. The section is closed by default, and its summary reads, for example, "in fade · out slide left · pulse", or "off". **Reset** clears all three slots. With several clips selected, each one keeps its own other slots. Preview leaves the range and Loop on until you clear them.

**Clip ▸ Motion ▸ Preview** does the same as the Preview button. With several clips selected, both loop the first selected clip that has a picture.

*Agents:* `set_video` with `motion: {in: {kind, duration}, out: {kind, duration}, during: {kind, amount, period}}` (durations and period in ticks, amount 0–1; `motion: null` clears all three).

### Entrances and exits

The same nine kinds fill both In and Out. An exit is the entrance played the other way: the In eases out as it arrives, and the Out eases in as it leaves.

| Kind | As an entrance (In) | As an exit (Out) |
|---|---|---|
| Fade | Fades in | Fades out |
| Zoom In | Grows from 60% to full size while fading in | Grows to 140% while fading out |
| Zoom Out | Shrinks from 140% to full size while fading in | Shrinks to 60% while fading out |
| Slide Left | Slides in from the right edge | Slides out past the left edge |
| Slide Right | Slides in from the left edge | Slides out past the right edge |
| Slide Up | Slides in from the bottom edge | Slides out past the top edge |
| Slide Down | Slides in from the top edge | Slides out past the bottom edge |
| Spin | Spins half a turn into place from 30% size, fading in | Spins half a turn away to 30% size, fading out |
| Pop | Springs up past full size (to about 110%) and settles, fading in over the first quarter | Swells and springs away, fading out over the last quarter |

A slide measures the layer as it is drawn, so it starts or ends exactly off the edge of the canvas (or of the nest it is inside).

### During

| Kind | What it does |
|---|---|
| Pulse | Gently grows and shrinks once per period, up to 20% larger at 100% |
| Shake | Jitters in a pattern that never visibly repeats, up to 4% of the canvas's shorter edge at 100% |
| Spin | Rotates continuously; at 50%, one full turn per period |
| Bounce | Hops upward once per period, up to 8% of the canvas height at 100% |
| Drift | A slow push-in across the whole clip, ending up to 24% larger at 100%. It ignores Period |

Every During movement starts from the clip's own placement on its first frame. It runs under the In and Out, so a clip can, for example, slide in while it pulses.

### On the timeline

A clip with an In or Out preset shows a small wedge along the bottom of its name strip, as long as the preset's duration at the current zoom. If the wedges overlap, the two presets are longer than the clip together. In that case Frame Job shortens both in proportion to their lengths, so the entrance ends on the frame where the exit begins, rather than refusing.

A clip with a During movement shows a small wave symbol at the right end of its name strip.

### Inactive presets

An In or Out with a zero duration can come from an agent or an older project. It is kept but does nothing. The section, the summary and the Motion menu mark it "(inactive)" (or "(some inactive)" across a selection), it draws no wedge, and a note reads "Selection includes inactive In motion (zero duration). Increase Duration to reactivate; choose None to clear."

### Limits

- A preset is not part of any action. Motion rows are ⊘, and edits always write the clip, even with an action selected.
- A split gives the first half no Out and the second half no In, so the cut doesn't play an exit and an entrance. A During movement restarts at each cut, so Remove Silences on a clip with Pulse or Drift can make it jump at the cuts.
- Freeze frame and Add Blurred Background drop the motion. Duplicate, Detach Audio and Paste keep it. Changing the speed doesn't rescale the presets.
- A text clip has no measured size, so a slide starts or ends half a canvas past the edge. That clears any text narrower than the canvas.
- A canvas drag started mid-motion starts from the clip's un-moved position.

221	/// `video.motion` (format version 8, road map 5's E2) — what a clip DOES on
222	/// its way in, on its way out, and all the way through.
223	///
224	/// The mirror of `core/src/model_motion.rs`, and the one property group in
225	/// the video patch that is not a quantity the compositor reads. The core
226	/// turns a preset into placement at render time — a layer's `scale`,
227	/// `rotation`, `opacity`, `x` and `y` — and the recipe publishes no
228	/// `motion` key at all, so nothing on this side draws it and nothing on
229	/// this side computes it. What lives here is the vocabulary: the two closed
230	/// enums, the two slot values, their display names and the dictionaries the
231	/// op layer sends.
232	///
233	/// **The dictionaries are here rather than in `ReelCore.swift`**, where
234	/// every other property type's `dictionary` extension sits, for the size
235	/// rule alone — that file is 1484 lines against the ~600 cap and may not
236	/// take a group's worth of new code. The types and their wire spelling are
237	/// one sentence, so they travel together.
238	///
239	/// **`MotionProps.dictionary` ALWAYS writes three keys**, `NSNull` for a
240	/// nil slot, and that is load-bearing rather than tidy: a core patch
241	/// DEEP-MERGES `motion` (`merge_group` → `actions::merge`), so a
242	/// `MotionProps` holding only an `in` sent as `{"in": …}` would leave a
243	/// stored `out` in place — choosing None from a popup would appear to do
244	/// nothing and beep. **This is the ONLY edge that replaces**, and since
245	/// D1·3 it is the only one that could be: an agent's `motion` goes to the
246	/// core as the caller wrote it and merges slot by slot like every other
247	/// nested object, so a whole object here is not a second rule but the same
248	/// rule spelled out by a writer that knows all three slots.
249	
250	// MARK: - Kinds
251	
252	/// The nine entrances and exits (`EdgeMotion`). One kind, read at an edge:
253	/// the same case means the mirrored thing on the way out — `zoomIn` grows
254	/// INTO the frame as an entrance and away from the viewer as an exit,
255	/// `slideLeft` enters from the right edge and leaves past the left one.
256	///
257	/// Closed, and decoded by RAW VALUE, so `JSONDecoder`'s
258	/// `.convertFromSnakeCase` never touches these spellings.
259	enum EdgeMotion: String, Codable, CaseIterable {
260	    case fade
261	    case zoomIn = "zoom_in"
262	    case zoomOut = "zoom_out"
263	    case slideLeft = "slide_left"
264	    case slideRight = "slide_right"
265	    case slideUp = "slide_up"
266	    case slideDown = "slide_down"
267	    case spin
268	    case pop
269	
270	    var displayName: String {
271	        switch self {
272	        case .fade: return "Fade"
273	        case .zoomIn: return "Zoom In"
274	        case .zoomOut: return "Zoom Out"
275	        case .slideLeft: return "Slide Left"
276	        case .slideRight: return "Slide Right"
277	        case .slideUp: return "Slide Up"
278	        case .slideDown: return "Slide Down"
279	        case .spin: return "Spin"
280	        case .pop: return "Pop"
281	        }
282	    }
283	}
284	
285	/// The five continuous motions (`DuringMotion`). Every one is the identity
286	/// at clip time 0, so a clip starts exactly where it is placed whatever it
287	/// goes on to do. `spin` is spelled in both enums, deliberately.
288	enum DuringMotion: String, Codable, CaseIterable {
289	    case pulse
290	    case shake
291	    case spin
292	    case bounce
293	    case drift
294	
295	    var displayName: String {
296	        switch self {
297	        case .pulse: return "Pulse"
298	        case .shake: return "Shake"
299	        case .spin: return "Spin"
300	        case .bounce: return "Bounce"
301	        case .drift: return "Drift"
302	        }
303	    }
304	}

308	/// One end of a clip: what it does, and for how long.
309	///
310	/// `duration` is a DURATION in ticks, not a time — an `in` measured forward
311	/// from the clip's first frame and an `out` back from its last — so
312	/// trimming a clip moves the preset with the edge it belongs to.
313	struct MotionEdge: Codable, Equatable {
314	    var kind: EdgeMotion
315	    var duration: Ticks
316	
317	    /// A zero duration keeps its stored kind but has no render-time effect.
318	    var isActive: Bool { duration > 0 }
319	
320	    var displayName: String {
321	        kind.displayName + (isActive ? "" : " (inactive)")
322	    }
323	
324	    /// The title of one kind across the selected edges of one slot.
325	    static func menuTitle(for kind: EdgeMotion, among edges: [MotionEdge?]) -> String {
326	        let matching = edges.compactMap { $0 }.filter { $0.kind == kind }
327	        guard matching.contains(where: { !$0.isActive }) else { return kind.displayName }
328	        let suffix = matching.contains(where: \.isActive) ? " (some inactive)" : " (inactive)"
329	        return kind.displayName + suffix
330	    }
331	
332	    /// The core's own default (`MotionEdge::default`): half a second of
333	    /// fade. Mirrored rather than derived, so switching a slot on writes
334	    /// exactly what the core would have defaulted to had the key simply
335	    /// appeared.
336	    init(kind: EdgeMotion = .fade, duration: Ticks = Ticks(ReelTime.perSecond) / 2) {
337	        self.kind = kind
338	        self.duration = duration
339	    }
340	
341	    init(from decoder: Decoder) throws {
342	        let c = try decoder.container(keyedBy: CodingKeys.self)
343	        kind = c.lenient(.kind, EdgeMotion.fade)
344	        duration = c.lenient(.duration, Ticks(ReelTime.perSecond) / 2)
345	    }
346	
347	    var dictionary: [String: Any] { ["kind": kind.rawValue, "duration": duration] }
348	}
349	
350	/// What a clip does for its whole length, under whatever its two edges are
351	/// doing. `amount` is 0–1 and `period` is one cycle in ticks; `drift`
352	/// ignores the period.
353	struct MotionDuring: Codable, Equatable {
354	    var kind: DuringMotion
355	    var amount: Double
356	    var period: Ticks
357	
358	    /// The core's own default (`MotionDuring::default`): a half-strength
359	    /// one-second pulse.
360	    init(
361	        kind: DuringMotion = .pulse, amount: Double = 0.5,
362	        period: Ticks = Ticks(ReelTime.perSecond)
363	    ) {
364	        self.kind = kind
365	        self.amount = amount
366	        self.period = period
367	    }
368	
369	    init(from decoder: Decoder) throws {
370	        let c = try decoder.container(keyedBy: CodingKeys.self)
371	        kind = c.lenient(.kind, DuringMotion.pulse)
372	        amount = c.lenient(.amount, 0.5)
373	        period = c.lenient(.period, Ticks(ReelTime.perSecond))
374	    }
375	
376	    var dictionary: [String: Any] {
377	        ["kind": kind.rawValue, "amount": amount, "period": period]
378	    }
379	}

381	// MARK: - The group
382	
383	/// The three slots, each `nil` when the clip does nothing of that sort.
384	///
385	/// `in` is a Swift keyword, so the entrance is `inEdge` here and the
386	/// model's key name lives in `CodingKeys` — `TextAnimation`'s arrangement,
387	/// for its reason. The key spelling is the contract with
388	/// `core/src/model_motion.rs`'s `#[serde(rename = "in")]`; the property
389	/// name is this side's business alone.
390	struct MotionProps: Codable, Equatable {
391	    /// The entrance (the model's `in`).
392	    var inEdge: MotionEdge?
393	    /// The exit.
394	    var out: MotionEdge?
395	    /// What the clip does for its whole length.
396	    var during: MotionDuring?
397	
398	    init(inEdge: MotionEdge? = nil, out: MotionEdge? = nil, during: MotionDuring? = nil) {
399	        self.inEdge = inEdge
400	        self.out = out
401	        self.during = during
402	    }
403	
404	    private enum CodingKeys: String, CodingKey {
405	        case inEdge = "in"
406	        case out
407	        case during
408	    }
409	
410	    init(from decoder: Decoder) throws {
411	        let c = try decoder.container(keyedBy: CodingKeys.self)
412	        inEdge = c.lenient(.inEdge)
413	        out = c.lenient(.out)
414	        during = c.lenient(.during)
415	    }
416	
417	    /// No slot filled — the state the core normalises to `null`, and what a
418	    /// writer sends as `motion: null` rather than as three nulls.
419	    var isEmpty: Bool { inEdge == nil && out == nil && during == nil }
420	
421	    /// ALWAYS three keys, `NSNull` for a nil slot. The type doc says why.
422	    var dictionary: [String: Any] {
423	        [
424	            "in": inEdge.map { $0.dictionary as Any } ?? NSNull(),
425	            "out": out.map { $0.dictionary as Any } ?? NSNull(),
426	            "during": during.map { $0.dictionary as Any } ?? NSNull(),
427	        ]
428	    }
429	}

433	/// A copy with `change` applied to it and everything `change` does not touch
434	/// kept — the step both the Motion section and Clip ▸ Motion take per clip,
435	/// because a `motion` patch replaces the whole object and a clip keeps its
436	/// own other slots.
437	extension MotionProps {
438	    func with(_ change: (inout MotionProps) -> Void) -> MotionProps {
439	        var next = self
440	        change(&next)
441	        return next
442	    }

496	    private enum MotionSlot {
497	        case inEdge, out, during

500	    /// The selected clips a motion applies to.

502	        guard let document = document else { return [] }

507	    private func setMotionCommand(slot: MotionSlot, sender: Any?) {
508	        let targets = motionTargets
509	        guard let document = document, let tag = (sender as? NSMenuItem)?.tag,
510	              !targets.isEmpty
511	        else {
512	            NSSound.beep()
513	            return
514	        }
515	        let count = slot == .during ? DuringMotion.allCases.count : EdgeMotion.allCases.count
516	        // None is EXACTLY −1, the one negative tag `motionSlotMenu` writes
517	        // (`AppDelegate+Menus.swift`). Any other tag out of range is a
518	        // stranger — an item nothing in this app built — and clearing a
519	        // person's arrival because a tag was −7 is a write they did not ask
520	        // for. It beeps and writes nothing.
521	        guard tag == Self.motionNoneTag || (tag >= 0 && tag < count) else {
522	            NSSound.beep()
523	            return
524	        }
525	        var ops: [ReelOp] = []
526	        for clip in targets {
527	            let current = clip.videoProps.motion ?? MotionProps()
528	            let next: MotionProps
529	            switch slot {
530	            case .inEdge:
531	                next = current.with { $0.inEdge = edge(tag, keeping: current.inEdge) }
532	            case .out:
533	                next = current.with { $0.out = edge(tag, keeping: current.out) }
534	            case .during:
535	                next = current.with { $0.during = during(tag, keeping: current.during) }
536	            }
537	            ops.append(.setVideo(clips: [clip.id], patch: VideoPatch(motion: .some(next))))
538	        }
539	        // Three answers, not two. An all-identity batch is the core's refusal
540	        // and beeps; a mixed one LANDS (`ReelProject.applying` runs later ops
541	        // past an identity). But `set_video` re-checks the whole stored group,
542	        // so a clip already carrying an out-of-range value — `paste` does not
543	        // range-check its payload — makes the op an `Err`, `applying` THROWS,
544	        // and the batch lands nothing and puts up the core's own message
545	        // (`core/tests/motion_edges.rs`'s
546	        // `a_motion_patch_on_a_clip_already_out_of_range_is_an_error`).

550	    /// A chosen kind keeps the slot's stored duration, else `MotionEdge()`'s
551	    /// 0.5 s — the section's rule. The caller's gate has already refused
552	    /// every tag but None and a real index, so `tag >= 0` is exactly "not

554	    private func edge(_ tag: Int, keeping stored: MotionEdge?) -> MotionEdge? {
555	        guard tag >= 0 else { return nil }
556	        let kind = EdgeMotion.allCases[tag]
557	        return MotionEdge(kind: kind, duration: stored?.duration ?? MotionEdge().duration)
558	    }

560	    /// A chosen kind keeps the stored amount and period, else the defaults.
561	    /// The caller's gate has already refused a stranger, as in [`edge`].
562	    private func during(_ tag: Int, keeping stored: MotionDuring?) -> MotionDuring? {
563	        guard tag >= 0 else { return nil }
564	        var next = stored ?? MotionDuring()
565	        next.kind = DuringMotion.allCases[tag]
566	        return next
567	    }

569	    /// The kind the targets agree on in one slot: `.some(kind)` when every
570	    /// target carries it, `.some(nil)` when none carries the slot, and nil
571	    /// when they disagree — `sharedClipLabel`'s shape, so a checkmark is on a
572	    /// kind, on None, or on nothing.

574	        let kinds = motionTargets.map { read($0.videoProps.motion) }
575	        guard let first = kinds.first, kinds.allSatisfy({ $0 == first }) else { return nil }

620	        return kinds.indices.contains(tag) ? .some(kinds[tag]) : nil

1	//! `video.motion` turned into PLACEMENT — road map 5 §5b–§5c's arithmetic,
2	//! and the only place in the crate that reads a preset.
3	//!
4	//! A preset says what a clip DOES; this says where it therefore IS at one
5	//! instant. [`apply`] takes the EVALUATED video props of a clip (actions
6	//! already applied), the clip time, the clip's own duration, the source's
7	//! pixel size and the container's canvas, and answers the same props with
8	//! five fields moved: `scale`, `rotation`, `opacity`, `x` and `y`. Every
9	//! other field passes through untouched, which is what lets `recipe.rs`
10	//! read a layer's per-pixel properties off the moved props without knowing
11	//! anything about motion.
12	//!
13	//! **It is called where placement is PRODUCED and nowhere else** (spec §11,
14	//! R5-4): the two call sites are `recipe.rs`'s `moved` (a clip's own, which
15	//! `layer` and the routed dissolve's `placement` read) and `frame_of`.
16	//! `evaluate_clip`, `clip_state`, `get_project`, `split_clip`'s state,
17	//! `add_zoom_action`, `freeze_frame` and the audio plan all read the clip
18	//! UN-MOVED, so an edit works on the numbers a person typed and only the
19	//! picture moves. A build that moved `evaluate_clip` instead would pass a
20	//! careless render check and break every edit.
21	//!
22	//! # The three slots
23	//!
24	//! An ARRIVAL runs for the first `in` of the clip on `a = ease_out(t/in′)`,
25	//! a DEPARTURE for the last `out` on `d = ease_in(v)` measured back from
26	//! the EXCLUSIVE end so the last drawn frame still shows a sliver
27	//! (`recipe_text.rs:150`'s convention), and a DURING runs for the whole
28	//! clip. Each yields a scale factor `F`, a rotation `φ` in degrees, an
29	//! opacity factor `O` and an offset `Δ` in canvas pixels; the totals are
30	//! `F = F_in·F_out·F_during`, `φ = Σφ`, `O = O_in·O_out` and `Δ = ΣΔ`.
31	//!
32	//! **The tent.** When `in + out > D` the two are scaled to meet —
33	//! `in′ = in·D/(in + out)`, `out′ = D − in′` — so the arrival ends on the
34	//! frame the departure begins and nothing refuses. "Too long for THIS clip"
35	//! is a fact about a clip, not about the vocabulary, and a later trim would
36	//! invalidate any refusal anyway.
37	//!
38	//! **Rotation is REDUCED.** `φ` is taken `rem_euclid(360)` before it is
39	//! added, so a whole turn is EXACTLY no turn. Without it a rotation of 360
40	//! would reach Swift as `Float(360·π/180)`, whose `sin` is ~1.7e-7 rather
41	//! than 0 (`Compositor.swift`), and `partnerBox`'s `rotation == 0` guard
42	//! would read the layer as rotated. `rem_euclid` alone is not enough — it
43	//! adds 360 to a negative remainder and a tiny negative one ROUNDS UP to
44	//! exactly 360, or to a double a hair under it, and that guard compares the
45	//! recipe's f64 to an EXACT 0, so either one reads as rotated. So a band under
46	//! a whole turn is published as no turn. The band CHOSEN is "rounds to 360 as
47	//! an f32 of degrees", 2⁻¹⁶ of a degree: no consumer reads degrees into an f32
48	//! (the one f32 is the uniform above, in RADIANS), and what justifies it is
49	//! that it moves the corner of a 4K frame, 2202.9 px from a centred pivot, by
50	//! at most 5.87e-4 px (`core/tests/motion_edges.rs`).
51	//!
52	//! **The pivot is the VISIBLE centre.** The core's placement rule (★,
53	//! `edit_zoom.rs`) pivots on the UNCROPPED anchor, so a zoom or a spin
54	//! about it would make a cropped layer drift across its own preset. The
55	//! moved position compensates:
56	//! `(x, y)′ = (x, y) + s·R(θ)·c − s″·R(θ″)·c + Δ`, with `c` the cropped
57	//! rect's centre in source pixels, `s″` the CLAMPED drawn scale and `θ″`
58	//! the drawn rotation. At `F = 1`, `φ = 0` the two terms are the same
59	//! expression and cancel to the bit, which is what makes an inactive
60	//! preset free.
61	//!
62	//! **Slides are measured against the DRAWN box.** `S_right` is the offset
63	//! that puts the layer's right edge exactly on the container's right edge,
64	//! measured at `s″` and `θ″` — the size actually drawn — from the BASE
65	//! visible centre `p = (x, y) + s·R(θ)·c`, which is where the pivot
66	//! compensation holds the layer whatever the other slots do. For TEXT the
67	//! core has no measured size (spec §11), so `hx = W/2`, `hy = H/2` and
68	//! `c = 0`: the anchor starts half a canvas beyond the edge, which clears
69	//! any text narrower than the canvas. Recorded as a limit.
70	//!
71	//! # It never trusts the file
72	//!
73	//! `validate` range-checks no property and `evaluate_clip`'s restore copies
74	//! the BASE motion past `clamp_video`, so a hand-written `period: 0`, a
75	//! negative duration or an `amount` of 5 arrives here. A slot whose
76	//! duration is ≤ 0 after the tent is inactive; a `during` whose `period` is
77	//! ≤ 0 is inactive; `amount` is clamped to 0…1; and every output is checked
78	//! finite, a non-finite one leaving that field as evaluated. No NaN reaches
79	//! the recipe.
80	//!
81	//! **And when nothing is active it SHORT-CIRCUITS**, returning
82	//! `video.clone()` rather than computing an identity. `x + b − b` is not
83	//! `x` in floats, and the frame at `in′` has to be byte-identical to the
84	//! same clip with no motion at all — which is the claim `core/tests/
85	//! motion.rs` makes and the one an export comparison rests on.
86	
87	use crate::model::{DuringMotion, EdgeMotion, Motion, MotionDuring, MotionEdge, VideoProps};

92	/// The overshoot curve `pop` is built on: above 1 from `u ≈ 0.37`, peaking
93	/// at 1.100 around `u ≈ 0.58`, back at exactly 1 when `u` is 1.
94	fn back_out(u: f64) -> f64 {
95	    let p = u - 1.0;
96	    1.0 + 2.70158 * p * p * p + 1.70158 * p * p
97	}
98	
99	/// Which container edge a slide measures itself against.
100	#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
101	enum Side {
102	    Left,
103	    Right,
104	    Top,
105	    Bottom,
106	}
107	
108	/// One slot's contribution, before the geometry a slide needs is known.
109	struct Term {
110	    f: f64,
111	    phi: f64,
112	    o: f64,
113	    /// A slide, as the edge it is measured from and the fraction of the way
114	    /// out to it — resolved once `F` and `φ` have fixed the drawn box.
115	    slide: Option<(Side, f64)>,
116	    /// A displacement in canvas pixels that needs no geometry at all.
117	    delta: (f64, f64),
118	}
119	
120	impl Term {
121	    /// The identity: nothing scaled, turned, faded or moved.
122	    const NONE: Term = Term {
123	        f: 1.0,
124	        phi: 0.0,
125	        o: 1.0,
126	        slide: None,
127	        delta: (0.0, 0.0),
128	    };
129	}

131	/// The arrival table (road map 5 §5b). `a` is the eased progress and `u`
132	/// the raw one, which only `pop` reads.
133	fn arrival(kind: EdgeMotion, a: f64, u: f64) -> Term {
134	    match kind {
135	        EdgeMotion::Fade => Term { o: a, ..Term::NONE },
136	        EdgeMotion::ZoomIn => Term {
137	            f: 0.6 + 0.4 * a,
138	            o: a,
139	            ..Term::NONE
140	        },
141	        EdgeMotion::ZoomOut => Term {
142	            f: 1.4 - 0.4 * a,
143	            o: a,
144	            ..Term::NONE
145	        },
146	        // A slide names the edge it comes FROM: `slide_left` moves left, so
147	        // it enters from the right.
148	        EdgeMotion::SlideLeft => Term {
149	            slide: Some((Side::Right, 1.0 - a)),
150	            ..Term::NONE
151	        },
152	        EdgeMotion::SlideRight => Term {
153	            slide: Some((Side::Left, 1.0 - a)),
154	            ..Term::NONE
155	        },
156	        EdgeMotion::SlideUp => Term {
157	            slide: Some((Side::Bottom, 1.0 - a)),
158	            ..Term::NONE
159	        },
160	        EdgeMotion::SlideDown => Term {
161	            slide: Some((Side::Top, 1.0 - a)),
162	            ..Term::NONE
163	        },
164	        EdgeMotion::Spin => Term {
165	            f: 0.3 + 0.7 * a,
166	            phi: -180.0 * (1.0 - a),
167	            o: a,
168	            ..Term::NONE
169	        },
170	        // The overshoot is the whole preset, so `pop` is the one arrival
171	        // measured on the RAW progress; its fade is over in the first
172	        // quarter, before the scale has passed 1.
173	        EdgeMotion::Pop => Term {
174	            f: back_out(u),
175	            o: (u / 0.25).min(1.0),
176	            ..Term::NONE
177	        },
178	    }
179	}
180	
181	/// The departure table (road map 5 §5b). `d` is the eased progress and `v`
182	/// the raw one; `1 − v` is how much of the exit is LEFT, which is what
183	/// `pop` runs backwards on.
184	fn departure(kind: EdgeMotion, d: f64, v: f64) -> Term {
185	    let left = 1.0 - v;
186	    match kind {
187	        EdgeMotion::Fade => Term {
188	            o: 1.0 - d,
189	            ..Term::NONE
190	        },
191	        EdgeMotion::ZoomIn => Term {
192	            f: 1.0 + 0.4 * d,
193	            o: 1.0 - d,
194	            ..Term::NONE
195	        },
196	        EdgeMotion::ZoomOut => Term {
197	            f: 1.0 - 0.4 * d,
198	            o: 1.0 - d,
199	            ..Term::NONE
200	        },
201	        // On the way out a slide names the edge it leaves PAST, which is
202	        // the mirror of the arrival above.
203	        EdgeMotion::SlideLeft => Term {
204	            slide: Some((Side::Left, d)),
205	            ..Term::NONE
206	        },
207	        EdgeMotion::SlideRight => Term {
208	            slide: Some((Side::Right, d)),
209	            ..Term::NONE
210	        },
211	        EdgeMotion::SlideUp => Term {
212	            slide: Some((Side::Top, d)),
213	            ..Term::NONE
214	        },
215	        EdgeMotion::SlideDown => Term {
216	            slide: Some((Side::Bottom, d)),
217	            ..Term::NONE
218	        },
219	        EdgeMotion::Spin => Term {
220	            f: 1.0 - 0.7 * d,
221	            phi: 180.0 * d,
222	            o: 1.0 - d,
223	            ..Term::NONE
224	        },
225	        EdgeMotion::Pop => Term {
226	            f: back_out(left),
227	            o: (left / 0.25).min(1.0),
228	            ..Term::NONE
229	        },
230	    }
231	}

233	/// The continuous table (road map 5 §5b). Every one of the five is the
234	/// IDENTITY at `t = 0`, so a clip starts exactly where it is placed.
235	fn during(
236	    kind: DuringMotion,
237	    amount: f64,
238	    t: f64,
239	    period: f64,
240	    duration: f64,
241	    w: f64,
242	    h: f64,
243	) -> Term {
244	    let cycles = t / period;
245	    match kind {
246	        DuringMotion::Pulse => Term {
247	            f: 1.0 + 0.2 * amount * (1.0 - (std::f64::consts::TAU * cycles).cos()) / 2.0,
248	            ..Term::NONE
249	        },
250	        // Two incommensurable sines per axis, so the shake never repeats
251	        // inside a period and never reads as a loop. `m` is the SHORT edge
252	        // of the container, so the displacement is the same fraction of the
253	        // picture whatever its aspect.
254	        DuringMotion::Shake => {
255	            let m = w.min(h);
256	            let wave = |k: f64| (std::f64::consts::TAU * k * cycles).sin();
257	            Term {
258	                delta: (
259	                    0.04 * amount * m * (0.6 * wave(1.0) + 0.4 * wave(2.7)),
260	                    0.04 * amount * m * (0.6 * wave(1.3) + 0.4 * wave(3.1)),
261	                ),
262	                ..Term::NONE
263	            }
264	        }
265	        // `amount` 0.5 is one whole turn per period, which is why the total
266	        // is reduced `rem_euclid(360)` by the caller rather than here: the
267	        // reduction has to see the SUM, or an edge spin plus a during spin
268	        // could land on a multiple of 360 and still read as turned.
269	        DuringMotion::Spin => Term {
270	            phi: 720.0 * amount * cycles,
271	            ..Term::NONE
272	        },
273	        DuringMotion::Bounce => Term {
274	            delta: (
275	                0.0,
276	                -0.08 * amount * h * (std::f64::consts::PI * cycles).sin().abs(),
277	            ),
278	            ..Term::NONE
279	        },
280	        // The one preset that ignores `period` entirely: a drift is a slow
281	        // push across the WHOLE clip, so its clock is the duration.
282	        DuringMotion::Drift => Term {
283	            f: 1.0 + 0.24 * amount * t / duration,
284	            ..Term::NONE
285	        },
286	    }
287	}

289	/// The two edge durations after the tent rule, in ticks as floats.
290	fn tent(motion: &Motion, duration: f64) -> (f64, f64) {
291	    let raw = |edge: &Option<MotionEdge>| edge.map_or(0.0, |e| e.duration as f64);
292	    let (mut arrive, mut leave) = (raw(&motion.r#in), raw(&motion.out));
293	    if arrive + leave > duration && arrive + leave > 0.0 {
294	        arrive = arrive * duration / (arrive + leave);
295	        leave = duration - arrive;
296	    }
297	    (arrive, leave)
298	}

300	/// A `during` slot that is actually running: `period` above zero, and a
301	/// duration to measure a drift against.
302	fn live_during(motion: &Motion, duration: f64) -> Option<(MotionDuring, f64, f64)> {
303	    let slot = motion.during?;
304	    let period = slot.period as f64;
305	    if period <= 0.0 || !period.is_finite() {
306	        return None;
307	    }
308	    // A drift divides by the clip's duration; every other kind ignores it.
309	    if matches!(slot.kind, DuringMotion::Drift) && duration <= 0.0 {
310	        return None;
311	    }
312	    let amount = if slot.amount.is_finite() {
313	        slot.amount.clamp(0.0, 1.0)
314	    } else {
315	        0.0
316	    };
317	    Some((slot, amount, period))
318	}

320	/// `video` with its five placed fields moved by whatever `video.motion`
321	/// asks for at `clip_t`. Every other field is the input's.
322	///
323	/// `size` is the source's pixel size (`Project::source_size`), `None` for
324	/// text; `container` is the canvas the clip is placed in — the project's,
325	/// or the frozen canvas of the nest it lives inside. See the module doc.
326	pub(crate) fn apply(
327	    video: &VideoProps,
328	    clip_t: Ticks,
329	    duration: Ticks,
330	    size: Option<(f64, f64)>,
331	    container: (f64, f64),
332	) -> VideoProps {
333	    let Some(motion) = video.motion else {
334	        return video.clone();
335	    };
336	    let t = clip_t as f64;
337	    let d = duration as f64;
338	    let (arrive, leave) = tent(&motion, d);
339	
340	    let arrival_term = motion.r#in.filter(|_| arrive > 0.0 && t < arrive).map(|e| {
341	        let u = t / arrive;
342	        arrival(
343	            e.kind,
344	            crate::actions::ease(crate::model::Curve::EaseOut, u),
345	            u,
346	        )
347	    });
348	    let departure_term = motion
349	        .out
350	        .filter(|_| leave > 0.0 && t >= d - leave)
351	        .map(|e| {
352	            let v = 1.0 - (d - t) / leave;
353	            departure(
354	                e.kind,
355	                crate::actions::ease(crate::model::Curve::EaseIn, v),
356	                v,
357	            )
358	        });
359	    let during_term = live_during(&motion, d).map(|(slot, amount, period)| {
360	        during(slot.kind, amount, t, period, d, container.0, container.1)
361	    });
362	
363	    // Nothing running: the clip is exactly where it is placed, and saying so
364	    // by cloning rather than by computing an identity is what makes the
365	    // frame byte-identical to a clip with no motion (module doc).
366	    if arrival_term.is_none() && departure_term.is_none() && during_term.is_none() {
367	        return video.clone();
368	    }
369	
370	    let terms = [&arrival_term, &departure_term, &during_term];
371	    let mut factor = 1.0_f64;
372	    let mut phi = 0.0_f64;
373	    let mut opacity_factor = 1.0_f64;
374	    let mut delta = (0.0_f64, 0.0_f64);
375	    for term in terms.iter().filter_map(|t| t.as_ref()) {
376	        factor *= term.f;
377	        phi += term.phi;
378	        delta.0 += term.delta.0;
379	        delta.1 += term.delta.1;
380	    }
381	    // Opacity is the two EDGES only — a during never fades, so folding the
382	    // third term in would be a factor of 1 that could still round.
383	    for term in [&arrival_term, &departure_term]
384	        .iter()
385	        .filter_map(|t| t.as_ref())
386	    {
387	        opacity_factor *= term.o;
388	    }
389	    let phi = if phi.is_finite() {
390	        // `rem_euclid` alone cannot keep the reduction's promise: it is
391	        // `let r = self % rhs; if r < 0.0 { r + rhs.abs() } else { r }`, and
392	        // for a φ of −2e-14 that addition ROUNDS UP to exactly 360.0 — the
393	        // one value the reduction exists to prevent. An arrival `spin` one
394	        // tick from its end produces exactly that φ.
395	        let reduced = phi.rem_euclid(360.0);
396	        // And a double merely NEAR 360 is no better than 360 itself, because
397	        // `Compositor.swift`'s `partnerBox` guard tests `rotation == 0`
398	        // EXACTLY, on the recipe's f64 (`RecipeLayer.rotation` is a `Double`):
399	        // a layer that is unrotated to the eye has to publish an exact zero,
400	        // and the same arrival one tick earlier reaches 359.99999999999994,
401	        // which fails that guard exactly as 360.0 does. So a BAND under a
402	        // whole turn is published as no turn. The band is CHOSEN, not read off
403	        // a consumer: "rounds to 360 as an f32 of DEGREES", a convenient
404	        // conservative width of 2⁻¹⁶ of a degree (1.5259e-5°). No f32 of
405	        // degrees exists anywhere: the one f32 is the Metal uniform,
406	        // `Float(rotation · π/180)`, RADIANS, which conflates only doubles
407	        // within 3.64e-6° of a turn (a band 4.2× narrower) and which the guard
408	        // never sees. What justifies the width is the PICTURE: 1.5259e-5°
409	        // moves the corner of a 4K frame (√(1920² + 1080²) = 2202.9 px from
410	        // its centre) by at most 5.87e-4 px. What the rule actually moves is
411	        // 1.998e-14° one tick from an arrival's end and 1.0e-5° at the
412	        // `during` `core/tests/motion_edges.rs` pins.
413	        if reduced as f32 >= 360.0 {
414	            0.0
415	        } else {
416	            reduced
417	        }
418	    } else {
419	        0.0
420	    };
421	
422	    let base_scale = if video.scale.is_finite() {
423	        video.scale
424	    } else {
425	        1.0
426	    };
427	    let base_rotation = if video.rotation.is_finite() {
428	        video.rotation
429	    } else {
430	        0.0
431	    };
432	    let drawn_scale = (base_scale * factor).clamp(SCALE_MIN, SCALE_MAX);
433	    let drawn_rotation = base_rotation + phi;
434	
435	    // The cropped rect's centre in source pixels (★'s `c`), and the visible
436	    // size the slide box is measured from. Text has neither, so it takes the
437	    // half-canvas rule the module doc records as a limit.
438	    let crop = video.crop;
439	    let (centre, half_x, half_y) = match size {
440	        Some((sw, sh)) => {
441	            let visible_w = (sw - crop.l - crop.r).max(0.0);
442	            let visible_h = (sh - crop.t - crop.b).max(0.0);
443	            let k = drawn_rotation.to_radians().cos().abs();
444	            let n = drawn_rotation.to_radians().sin().abs();
445	            (
446	                ((crop.l - crop.r) / 2.0, (crop.t - crop.b) / 2.0),

## Motion presets

A motion preset says what a clip **does** rather than where it is. Each clip has three slots: an **In** (an entrance at its start), an **Out** (an exit at its end) and a **During** (a movement for its whole length). A preset is tied to the clip's ends, so it moves with a trim. It works on any clip that draws a picture: video, still images, text, shapes, graphics and nests.

Motion is applied on top of the clip's own placement and any actions, and it is never animated by an action. A preset works relative to the clip: its scale and opacity multiply the clip's own, and its rotation and offset add to them. Zoom and Spin turn about the clip's visible centre, after any crop. The inspector fields (and `get_project`) show the clip's own, un-moved values, even though the preview and export show it moving.

### Set a preset

Use the **Motion presets** section at the end of the Clip sub-tab, or **Clip ▸ Motion ▸ In**, **Out** or **During**. Each submenu lists the kinds, then **None** to clear the slot. A checkmark shows the kind every selected clip shares.

The section's rows:

| Row | What it does | Range | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| In | The entrance kind, or None | None and nine kinds | None |
| In Duration | How long the entrance takes (disabled with None) | 0.1–10 s (quick picks 0.25, 0.5, 1) | 0.5 s |
| Out | The exit kind, or None | None and nine kinds | None |
| Out Duration | How long the exit takes (disabled with None) | 0.1–10 s (quick picks 0.25, 0.5, 1) | 0.5 s |
| During | The continuous movement, or None | None and five kinds | None |
| Amount | How strong the During movement is (disabled with None) | 0–100% (quick picks 25, 50, 75, 100) | 50% |
| Period | How long one cycle takes (disabled with None and for Drift) | 0.1–10 s (quick picks 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2) | 1 s |
| Preview | Sets the in/out range to the clip, turns Loop on and plays it | | |

Changing a slot's kind keeps the duration, amount and period it already had. The section is closed by default, and its summary reads, for example, "in fade · out slide left · pulse", or "off". **Reset** clears all three slots. With several clips selected, each one keeps its own other slots. Preview leaves the range and Loop on until you clear them.

**Clip ▸ Motion ▸ Preview** does the same as the Preview button. With several clips selected, both loop the first selected clip that has a picture.

*Agents:* `set_video` with `motion: {in: {kind, duration}, out: {kind, duration}, during: {kind, amount, period}}` (durations and period in ticks, amount 0–1; `motion: null` clears all three).

### Entrances and exits

The same nine kinds fill both In and Out. An exit is the entrance played the other way: the In eases out as it arrives, and the Out eases in as it leaves.

| Kind | As an entrance (In) | As an exit (Out) |
|---|---|---|
| Fade | Fades in | Fades out |
| Zoom In | Grows from 60% to full size while fading in | Grows to 140% while fading out |
| Zoom Out | Shrinks from 140% to full size while fading in | Shrinks to 60% while fading out |
| Slide Left | Slides in from the right edge | Slides out past the left edge |
| Slide Right | Slides in from the left edge | Slides out past the right edge |
| Slide Up | Slides in from the bottom edge | Slides out past the top edge |
| Slide Down | Slides in from the top edge | Slides out past the bottom edge |
| Spin | Spins half a turn into place from 30% size, fading in | Spins half a turn away to 30% size, fading out |
| Pop | Springs up past full size (to about 110%) and settles, fading in over the first quarter | Swells and springs away, fading out over the last quarter |

A slide measures the layer as it is drawn, so it starts or ends exactly off the edge of the canvas (or of the nest it is inside).

### During

| Kind | What it does |
|---|---|
| Pulse | Gently grows and shrinks once per period, up to 20% larger at 100% |
| Shake | Jitters in a pattern that never visibly repeats, up to 4% of the canvas's shorter edge at 100% |
| Spin | Rotates continuously; at 50%, one full turn per period |
| Bounce | Hops upward once per period, up to 8% of the canvas height at 100% |
| Drift | A slow push-in across the whole clip, ending up to 24% larger at 100%. It ignores Period |

Every During movement starts from the clip's own placement on its first frame. It runs under the In and Out, so a clip can, for example, slide in while it pulses.

### On the timeline

A clip with an In or Out preset shows a small wedge along the bottom of its name strip, as long as the preset's duration at the current zoom. If the wedges overlap, the two presets are longer than the clip together. In that case Frame Job shortens both in proportion to their lengths, so the entrance ends on the frame where the exit begins, rather than refusing.

A clip with a During movement shows a small wave symbol at the right end of its name strip.

### Inactive presets

An In or Out with a zero duration can come from an agent or an older project. It is kept but does nothing. The section, the summary and the Motion menu mark it "(inactive)" (or "(some inactive)" across a selection), it draws no wedge, and a note reads "Selection includes inactive In motion (zero duration). Increase Duration to reactivate; choose None to clear."

### Limits

- A preset is not part of any action. Motion rows are ⊘, and edits always write the clip, even with an action selected.
- A split gives the first half no Out and the second half no In, so the cut doesn't play an exit and an entrance. A During movement restarts at each cut, so Remove Silences on a clip with Pulse or Drift can make it jump at the cuts.
- Freeze frame and Add Blurred Background drop the motion. Duplicate, Detach Audio and Paste keep it. Changing the speed doesn't rescale the presets.
- A text clip has no measured size, so a slide starts or ends half a canvas past the edge. That clears any text narrower than the canvas.
- A canvas drag started mid-motion starts from the clip's un-moved position.

    private func drawMotionWedges(
        _ motion: MotionProps, clip: ClipSnapshot, strip: CGRect, body: CGRect
    ) {
        let perTick = body.width / CGFloat(max(clip.duration, 1))
        // 2 pt minimum so a short preset still shows; never wider than the clip.
        func width(_ edge: MotionEdge) -> CGFloat {
            min(max(CGFloat(edge.duration) * perTick, 2), body.width)
        }
        // 0.55 white: a strip literal, a shade under the icon's 0.62.
        NSColor.white.withAlphaComponent(0.55).setFill()
        if let edge = motion.inEdge, edge.isActive {
            let w = width(edge)
            let path = NSBezierPath()
            path.move(to: CGPoint(x: strip.minX, y: strip.maxY))
            path.line(to: CGPoint(x: strip.minX + w, y: strip.maxY))
            path.line(to: CGPoint(x: strip.minX + w, y: strip.maxY - 4))
            path.close()
            path.fill()
        }
        if let edge = motion.out, edge.isActive {
            let w = width(edge)
            let path = NSBezierPath()
            path.move(to: CGPoint(x: strip.maxX, y: strip.maxY))
            path.line(to: CGPoint(x: strip.maxX - w, y: strip.maxY))
            path.line(to: CGPoint(x: strip.maxX - w, y: strip.maxY - 4))
            path.close()
            path.fill()
        }
    }

Click **Loop**, the repeat button at the end of the transport in the toolbar. The button is dimmed while Loop is off and full strength while it's on. Click it again to turn Loop off.

---
title: Motion presets
description: Give a clip a ready-made entrance, exit or continuous movement that's tied to its two ends and stays with it through a trim.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A motion preset says what a clip does rather than where it is: how it arrives, how it leaves and what it does in between. It's tied to the clip's two ends, so it goes with the clip through a trim and there's nothing to reposition afterwards.

Each clip has three slots, and all three can run on the same clip:

- **In** is an entrance at the clip's start. See [Entrance and exit presets](/motion/entrances-and-exits/).
- **Out** is an exit at the clip's end, from the same nine kinds.
- **During** is a movement for the clip's whole length. See [During presets](/motion/during-presets/).

Presets work on any clip that draws a picture: video, still images, text, shapes, graphics and nests.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Clip ▸ Motion ▸ In', 'Clip ▸ Motion ▸ Out', 'Clip ▸ Motion ▸ During', 'Clip ▸ Motion ▸ Preview']}
  where="Clip tab ▸ Clip sub-tab ▸ Motion presets"
  tools="set_video"
/>

## Give a clip a preset

<Steps>

1. Select the clip.

2. In the Clip tab, pick the **Clip** sub-tab and open **Motion presets**, the last section. It's closed until you open it.

3. Choose a kind from **In**, **Out** or **During**.

4. Set **In Duration** or **Out Duration**, or for a During movement, **Amount** and **Period**.

5. Choose **Preview** to watch it loop.

</Steps>

If the defaults suit you, [the Motion menu](#use-the-motion-menu) is quicker.

## The Motion presets section

| Row | What it does | Range | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **In** | How the clip enters. | None and nine kinds | None |
| **In Duration** | How long the entrance takes. Dimmed while **In** is None. | 0.1 to 10 s, with quick picks of 0.25, 0.5 and 1 | 0.5 s |
| **Out** | How the clip leaves. | None and nine kinds | None |
| **Out Duration** | How long the exit takes. Dimmed while **Out** is None. | 0.1 to 10 s, with quick picks of 0.25, 0.5 and 1 | 0.5 s |
| **During** | What the clip does for its whole length. | None and five kinds | None |
| **Amount** | How strong the During movement is. Dimmed while **During** is None. | 0 to 100%, with quick picks of 25, 50, 75 and 100 | 50% |
| **Period** | How long one cycle of the During movement takes. Dimmed while **During** is None, and for Drift, which has no cycle. | 0.1 to 10 s, with quick picks of 0.25, 0.5, 1 and 2 | 1 s |
| **Preview** | Loops the clip so you can [watch its motion](#preview-a-preset). | | |

The two durations and **Period** snap to the project's frame grid. The In is measured from the clip's first frame and the Out back from its last.

With the section closed, its header sums up the clip's presets, for example "in fade · out slide left · pulse". With no presets it reads "off".

## Use the Motion menu

**Clip ▸ Motion** has three submenus, **In**, **Out** and **During**. Each lists its kinds, then **None** to clear the slot. They work on every selected clip that has a picture, and they're dimmed when no selected clip has one. None of them has a keyboard shortcut.

A checkmark shows the kind every selected clip shares. If the clips disagree, nothing is checked. If none of them has a preset in that slot, **None** is checked.

## Change or clear a preset

Choosing a different kind keeps the settings the slot already had: an In or Out keeps its duration, and a During keeps its amount and period. A slot you fill for the first time starts at the defaults, 0.5 s for an In or Out, and 50% with a 1 s period for a During.

To clear one slot, choose **None**. To clear all three, choose **Reset** in the section's header. **Reset** shows only when the clip has a preset to clear, and it clears every selected clip.

Each change is one undo step, however many clips are selected.

## Set presets on several clips

With several clips selected, a change to one slot leaves each clip's other slots as they were. Choosing a new In kind doesn't touch anyone's Out, and each clip keeps its own In duration.

The section shows the first selected clip's values, with **mixed** beside a row where the clips differ. That has two effects to watch for:

- **In Duration**, **Out Duration**, **Amount** and **Period** only change the clips that have a preset in that slot. The others are left alone.
- Those rows are dimmed by the first clip alone. If the first selected clip has no In, **In Duration** is dimmed even when other selected clips have one.

## Preview a preset

Choose **Preview** in the section, or **Clip ▸ Motion ▸ Preview**. Frame Job sets the [in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/) to the clip, turns [Loop](/timeline/loop/) on, moves the playhead to the clip's start and plays.

With several clips selected, it loops the first selected clip that has a picture.

The range and Loop stay until you clear them. Choose **Mark ▸ Clear Range** (<kbd>⌥X</kbd>) and click the **Loop** button in the toolbar. A range you'd already set is replaced.

## Read presets on the timeline

Small marks on a clip's name strip show its presets:

- **A wedge at each end** along the bottom of the strip stands for an In or an Out. It's as long as the preset's duration at the current zoom, and at least 2 points wide so a short preset still shows. The Clip tab's [action lane](/motion/action-lane/) shows the same two wedges.
- **A wave symbol** at the right end of the strip stands for a During movement. On a clip too narrow to fit it, the symbol is left out.

See [Reading a clip on the timeline](/timeline/reading-a-clip/) for everything else a clip draws.

## Motion sits on top of placement

A preset works relative to the clip. Frame Job takes the clip's own placement and any [actions](/motion/actions/) first, then applies the preset on top:

- Its scale and opacity multiply the clip's own. A clip at 50% opacity fades in to 50%, not 100%.
- Its rotation and offset add to the clip's own.
- Anything that changes the clip's size or turns it does so about the clip's visible centre, after any crop.
- The drawn size stays within the 1% to 1,000% that **Scale** allows.

The three slots add up the same way, so a clip can slide in while it pulses.

### The inspector shows un-moved values

The fields in the Clip tab show the clip's own numbers, even while the preview and the export show it moving. Halfway through a Zoom In, **Scale** still reads what you typed. That's why editing a clip's position or size works the same with a preset on it.

### Dragging during motion

A drag on the canvas changes the clip's own position, starting from where it sits without the preset. If you drag partway through a preset, the distance you drag is added to that un-moved position, and the preset keeps playing on top of it. To place a clip by eye, park the playhead where its In has finished and its Out hasn't started.

## Overlong presets shorten

When an In and an Out together last longer than the clip, Frame Job doesn't refuse them. It shortens both in proportion to their lengths, so the entrance ends on the frame where the exit begins. A 2 s In and a 1 s Out on a 1.5 s clip play as 1 s and 0.5 s. An In or Out alone that's longer than the clip plays over the clip's whole length.

On the timeline the wedges keep their full length, so they overlap. That's how to spot it. **In Duration** and **Out Duration** keep what you set too, so if you lengthen the clip later, the presets get their full time back.

## Inactive presets

An In or Out with a zero duration can come from an agent or an older project. Frame Job keeps it but it does nothing, and it draws no wedge. It's marked so you can fix it:

- The section's summary reads, for example, "in fade (inactive)".
- The **Clip ▸ Motion** submenus read **Fade (inactive)**, or **Fade (some inactive)** when only some of the selected clips with that kind have a zero duration.
- A note at the top of the section reads "Selection includes inactive In motion (zero duration). Increase Duration to reactivate; choose None to clear." It names **In**, **Out** or **In and Out**, and it counts every selected clip.

Changing the kind doesn't fix it, because a new kind keeps the old duration. Raise **In Duration** or **Out Duration**, or choose **None**.

## Presets and actions

An [action](/motion/actions/) animates a property to a value you set, over a span you place on the clip. A preset is anchored to the clip's ends and says what the clip does. Use a preset for an entrance, an exit or a repeating movement, and an action when a value has to reach a particular number at a particular moment.

A preset is never part of an action, and no action can animate one. While an action is selected, the section's rows are marked ⊘ and the section reads "Actions don't animate this. Edits here change the clip." Your edits there write the clip, as they do with no action selected, and **Reset** is still available.

## How edits treat a preset

| Edit | What happens to the presets |
| --- | --- |
| Trim | Each preset moves with its edge and keeps its length. |
| [Split](/editing/splitting/) | The first half keeps the In and gives up the Out, and the second half keeps the Out and gives up the In, so the cut doesn't play an exit and an entrance. Both halves keep the During. |
| [Change the speed](/speed/change-speed/) | The presets aren't rescaled. A 0.5 s In stays 0.5 s, and a clip that gets much shorter can make its presets [shorten](#overlong-presets-shorten). |
| [Freeze frame](/speed/freeze-frame/) | The still has no preset, and it sits at the clip's un-moved position, so a freeze taken mid-motion can jump. |
| [Add Blurred Background](/canvas/blurred-background/) | The backdrop copy doesn't move. The clip in front keeps its presets. |
| [Duplicate](/editing/duplicate-clips/), [Detach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/) and [Paste](/editing/copy-and-paste/) | The presets are kept. |
| [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/) | Presets are copied with the rest of the picture settings. |

A During movement restarts at each cut, because each piece is a clip of its own. [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) on a clip with Pulse or Drift can make it jump at the cuts.

## Good to know

- A preset moves the picture only. A Fade leaves the sound as it is, so use [audio fades](/audio/fades/) for that.
- A preset on a [nest](/editing/nests/) moves everything inside the nest together.
- [Adjustment clips](/color/adjustment-clips/) have the section and draw the marks, but a preset on one does nothing.
- [Motion blur](/motion/motion-blur/) blurs a preset's movement like any other.
- [Zoom to Region](/motion/zoom-to-region/) works out its zoom without a During movement, and tells you so with "This clip has During motion — the zoom is solved without it".
- [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/) works on an upright picture, so it won't take a clip with Spin in any slot.
- Changing the project's frame rate moves the durations and the period onto the new frame grid.

## With an agent

An agent sets and clears presets with `set_video`. It can change one slot and leave the others alone, or clear all three at once.

An agent isn't held to the section's ranges. Any duration of zero or more is accepted, which is how an [inactive preset](#inactive-presets) comes about, and a period can be outside 0.1 to 10 s as long as it isn't zero. An amount outside 0 to 100% is refused.

`get_project` answers the clip's un-moved values, so use `render_frame` to see a preset's effect. `set_action_end` won't take a preset, not even to clear one. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/).

## Related

- [Entrance and exit presets](/motion/entrances-and-exits/)
- [During presets](/motion/during-presets/)
- [Actions](/motion/actions/)
- [Transitions](/motion/transitions/)
- [The Clip menu](/reference/clip-menu/)

| **Period** | How long one cycle of the During movement takes. Dimmed while **During** is None, and for Drift, which has no cycle. | 0.1 to 10 s, with quick picks of 0.25, 0.5, 1 and 2 | 1 s |
| **Preview** | Loops the clip so you can [watch its motion](#preview-a-preset). | | |

The two durations and **Period** snap to the project's frame grid. The In is measured from the clip's first frame and the Out back from its last.

With the section closed, its header sums up the clip's presets, for example "in fade · out slide left · pulse". With no presets it reads "off".

## Use the Motion menu

**Clip ▸ Motion** has three submenus, **In**, **Out** and **During**. Each lists its kinds, then **None** to clear the slot. They work on every selected clip that has a picture, and they're dimmed when no selected clip has one. None of them has a keyboard shortcut.

A checkmark shows the kind every selected clip shares. If the clips disagree, nothing is checked. If none of them has a preset in that slot, **None** is checked.

## Change or clear a preset

Choosing a different kind keeps the settings the slot already had: an In or Out keeps its duration, and a During keeps its amount and period. A slot you fill for the first time starts at the defaults, 0.5 s for an In or Out, and 50% with a 1 s period for a During.

To clear one slot, choose **None**. To clear all three, choose **Reset** in the section's header. **Reset** shows only when the clip has a preset to clear, and it clears every selected clip.

Each change is one undo step, however many clips are selected.

## Set presets on several clips

With several clips selected, a change to one slot leaves each clip's other slots as they were. Choosing a new In kind doesn't touch anyone's Out, and each clip keeps its own In duration.

The section shows the first selected clip's values, with **mixed** beside a row where the clips differ. That has two effects to watch for:

- **In Duration**, **Out Duration**, **Amount** and **Period** only change the clips that have a preset in that slot. The others are left alone.
- Those rows are dimmed by the first clip alone. If the first selected clip has no In, **In Duration** is dimmed even when other selected clips have one.

## Preview a preset

Choose **Preview** in the section, or **Clip ▸ Motion ▸ Preview**. Frame Job sets the [in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/) to the clip, turns [Loop](/timeline/loop/) on, moves the playhead to the clip's start and plays.

With several clips selected, it loops the first selected clip that has a picture.

The range and Loop stay until you clear them. Choose **Mark ▸ Clear Range** (<kbd>⌥X</kbd>) and click the **Loop** button in the toolbar. A range you'd already set is replaced.

## Read presets on the timeline

Small marks on a clip's name strip show its presets:

- **A wedge at each end** along the bottom of the strip stands for an In or an Out. It's as long as the preset's duration at the current zoom, and at least 2 points wide so a short preset still shows. The Clip tab's [action lane](/motion/action-lane/) shows the same two wedges.
- **A wave symbol** at the right end of the strip stands for a During movement. On a clip too narrow to fit it, the symbol is left out.

See [Reading a clip on the timeline](/timeline/reading-a-clip/) for everything else a clip draws.

## Motion sits on top of placement

A preset works relative to the clip. Frame Job takes the clip's own placement and any [actions](/motion/actions/) first, then applies the preset on top:

- Its scale and opacity multiply the clip's own. A clip at 50% opacity fades in to 50%, not 100%.
- Its rotation and offset add to the clip's own.
- Anything that changes the clip's size or turns it does so about the clip's visible centre, after any crop.
- The drawn size stays within the 1% to 1,000% that **Scale** allows.

The three slots add up the same way, so a clip can slide in while it pulses.

### The inspector shows un-moved values

The fields in the Clip tab show the clip's own numbers, even while the preview and the export show it moving. Halfway through a Zoom In, **Scale** still reads what you typed. That's why editing a clip's position or size works the same with a preset on it.

### Dragging during motion

A drag on the canvas changes the clip's own position, starting from where it sits without the preset. If you drag partway through a preset, the distance you drag is added to that un-moved position, and the preset keeps playing on top of it. To place a clip by eye, park the playhead where its In has finished and its Out hasn't started.

## Overlong presets shorten

When an In and an Out together last longer than the clip, Frame Job doesn't refuse them. It shortens both in proportion to their lengths, so the entrance ends on the frame where the exit begins. A 2 s In and a 1 s Out on a 1.5 s clip play as 1 s and 0.5 s. An In or Out alone that's longer than the clip plays over the clip's whole length.

On the timeline the wedges keep their full length, so they overlap. That's how to spot it. **In Duration** and **Out Duration** keep what you set too, so if you lengthen the clip later, the presets get their full time back.

## Inactive presets

An In or Out with a zero duration can come from an agent or an older project. Frame Job keeps it but it does nothing, and it draws no wedge. It's marked so you can fix it:

- The section's summary reads, for example, "in fade (inactive)".
- The **Clip ▸ Motion** submenus read **Fade (inactive)**, or **Fade (some inactive)** when only some of the selected clips with that kind have a zero duration.
- A note at the top of the section reads "Selection includes inactive In motion (zero duration). Increase Duration to reactivate; choose None to clear." It names **In**, **Out** or **In and Out**, and it counts every selected clip.

Changing the kind doesn't fix it, because a new kind keeps the old duration. Raise **In Duration** or **Out Duration**, or choose **None**.

## Presets and actions

An [action](/motion/actions/) animates a property to a value you set, over a span you place on the clip. A preset is anchored to the clip's ends and says what the clip does. Use a preset for an entrance, an exit or a repeating movement, and an action when a value has to reach a particular number at a particular moment.

A preset is never part of an action, and no action can animate one. While an action is selected, the section's rows are marked ⊘ and the section reads "Actions don't animate this. Edits here change the clip." Your edits there write the clip, as they do with no action selected, and **Reset** is still available.

## How edits treat a preset

| Edit | What happens to the presets |
| --- | --- |
| Trim | Each preset moves with its edge and keeps its length. |
| [Split](/editing/splitting/) | The first half keeps the In and gives up the Out, and the second half keeps the Out and gives up the In, so the cut doesn't play an exit and an entrance. Both halves keep the During. |
| [Change the speed](/speed/change-speed/) | The presets aren't rescaled. A 0.5 s In stays 0.5 s, and a clip that gets much shorter can make its presets [shorten](#overlong-presets-shorten). |
| [Freeze frame](/speed/freeze-frame/) | The still has no preset, and it sits at the clip's un-moved position, so a freeze taken mid-motion can jump. |
| [Add Blurred Background](/canvas/blurred-background/) | The backdrop copy doesn't move. The clip in front keeps its presets. |
| [Duplicate](/editing/duplicate-clips/), [Detach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/) and [Paste](/editing/copy-and-paste/) | The presets are kept. |
| [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/) | Presets are copied with the rest of the picture settings. |

A During movement restarts at each cut, because each piece is a clip of its own. [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) on a clip with Pulse or Drift can make it jump at the cuts.

## Good to know

- A preset moves the picture only. A Fade leaves the sound as it is, so use [audio fades](/audio/fades/) for that.
- A preset on a [nest](/editing/nests/) moves everything inside the nest together.
- [Adjustment clips](/color/adjustment-clips/) have the section and draw the marks, but a preset on one does nothing.
- [Motion blur](/motion/motion-blur/) blurs a preset's movement like any other.
- [Zoom to Region](/motion/zoom-to-region/) works out its zoom without a During movement, and tells you so with "This clip has During motion — the zoom is solved without it".
- [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/) works on an upright picture, so it won't take a clip with Spin in any slot.
- Changing the project's frame rate moves the durations and the period onto the new frame grid.

## With an agent

An agent sets and clears presets with `set_video`. It can change one slot and leave the others alone, or clear all three at once.

An agent isn't held to the section's ranges. Any duration of zero or more is accepted, which is how an [inactive preset](#inactive-presets) comes about, and a period can be outside 0.1 to 10 s as long as it isn't zero. An amount outside 0 to 100% is refused.

`get_project` answers the clip's un-moved values, so use `render_frame` to see a preset's effect. `set_action_end` won't take a preset, not even to clear one. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/).

## Related

- [Entrance and exit presets](/motion/entrances-and-exits/)
- [During presets](/motion/during-presets/)
- [Actions](/motion/actions/)
- [Transitions](/motion/transitions/)
- [The Clip menu](/reference/clip-menu/)
