---
title: Entrance and exit presets
description: What each of the nine In and Out presets does, from Fade to Pop, and how a slide works out where to start and stop.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

The same nine kinds fill a clip's **In** and **Out** slots. This page says what each one does at each end. To set one, see [Motion presets](/motion/motion-presets/).

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Clip ▸ Motion ▸ In', 'Clip ▸ Motion ▸ Out']}
  where="Clip tab ▸ Clip sub-tab ▸ Motion presets"
  tools="set_video"
/>

## How In and Out relate

An exit is the entrance played the other way. An In starts quickly and slows as the clip arrives. An Out starts slowly and speeds up as the clip leaves. Pop is the exception, because it has a spring of its own.

Sizes here are relative to the clip's own size, and fades to its own opacity. A clip placed at 50% scale that zooms in from 60% starts at 30%. See [Motion sits on top of placement](/motion/motion-presets/#motion-sits-on-top-of-placement).

## Fade

The clip's opacity changes and nothing else does.

- **As an In:** fades in from fully transparent.
- **As an Out:** fades out.

## Zoom In

The clip grows, whichever end it's at.

- **As an In:** grows from 60% to full size while fading in.
- **As an Out:** grows to 140% while fading out.

## Zoom Out

The clip shrinks, whichever end it's at.

- **As an In:** shrinks from 140% to full size while fading in.
- **As an Out:** shrinks to 60% while fading out.

## Slide Left

A slide names the direction the clip travels. It doesn't fade, so the clip stays at full opacity the whole way. This one travels left.

- **As an In:** slides in from the right edge.
- **As an Out:** slides out past the left edge.

## Slide Right

- **As an In:** slides in from the left edge.
- **As an Out:** slides out past the right edge.

## Slide Up

- **As an In:** slides in from the bottom edge.
- **As an Out:** slides out past the top edge.

## Slide Down

- **As an In:** slides in from the top edge.
- **As an Out:** slides out past the bottom edge.

## Spin

The clip makes half a turn, clockwise at both ends.

- **As an In:** spins half a turn into place, growing from 30% size and fading in.
- **As an Out:** spins half a turn away, shrinking to 30% size and fading out.

## Pop

The clip springs past full size, so this is the one to use when you want a bounce.

- **As an In:** grows from nothing, overshoots to about 110% and settles at full size. It fades in over the first quarter of its duration.
- **As an Out:** swells to about 110%, then shrinks to nothing. It fades out over the last quarter.

## How slides measure

A slide measures the clip as it's drawn, with its scale, rotation and crop, from wherever you've placed it. So it starts or ends exactly off the edge of the canvas, however large the clip is and wherever it sits.

Inside a [nest](/editing/nests/), that edge is the nest's own canvas rather than the project's.

## Slides on text

A text clip has no measured size, so a slide can't work out exactly where it leaves the canvas. It starts or ends half a canvas past the edge instead. That clears any text narrower than the canvas. Text wider than the canvas can still show at the start of a slide in or the end of a slide out.

## Good to know

- An Out's last frame still shows a sliver of the movement, because the exit finishes at the end of that frame. A Fade out isn't fully transparent on the clip's very last frame.
- Every kind works with every During movement, so a clip can slide in while it pulses. See [During presets](/motion/during-presets/).
- A preset only moves the picture. For sound, see [Audio fades](/audio/fades/).

## Related

- [Motion presets](/motion/motion-presets/)
- [During presets](/motion/during-presets/)
- [Transitions](/motion/transitions/)

# CLAUDE.md — the documentation site

The public user documentation: Astro with Starlight, one page per feature or tight family of
features. `pnpm` manages it, Node is pinned by `.node-version`. `README.md` has the commands.

## Where things are

```
astro.config.mjs        Starlight's settings: title, logo, fonts, theme, plugins
sidebar.mjs             every page's place in the navigation, in order
src/content/docs/       the pages: <section>/<page>.mdx
src/data/features.json  THE FEATURE LIST: what /features/ renders and what the proof reads
src/components/         AtAGlance (a page's facts), Shot (a screen in both looks),
                        FeatureIndex (the filterable list)
src/assets/screens/     WebP captures, written only by scripts/import-screens.mjs
src/styles/             the brand: the mark's inks, the app's faces, square chrome
```

## The rule that matters

**Every claim is written from the code.** A label, a default, a range, a shortcut, a limit or a
refusal is checked against `app/Sources/`, `core/src/`, `graphic/` or `mcp-proxy/` before it is
written, and the code wins over `docs/guide/`, a spec or an ADR. Never write what a feature
probably does. If the code cannot settle it, leave it out.

Nothing dev-only, deferred or unbuilt is documented. That excludes the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`,
`perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`,
`loudness_meter`, `land_recording`, `analysis_job`, `transcript_view`, `playback_rebuilds`,
`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.

## Who reads this

Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.

So a page never mentions: spec or decision IDs (`AU-12`, `§11`), road maps, phases, issue numbers,
source file or type names, `rc_*` exports, format version numbers, proofs, tests, or the history
of a feature. Internal words get translated: "refused" becomes what the user sees ("Frame Job
won't do this while…"), "the core" and "the op" disappear. A tool name is the one exception: the
MCP pages and `tools=` in `AtAGlance` name agent tools, because those are the product's interface.

## Voice

- Plain, direct and second person. Say what it does, then how. Short sentences.
- Open with what the feature is for, in a sentence or two, before any steps.
- British spelling in prose, as `docs/guide/` does (colour, centre, grey, normalise), and the
  app's exact spelling for its own labels (the **Color** tab, **Normalize**).
- Contractions are fine. No marketing: never "powerful", "seamless", "effortless", "robust",
  "simply", "just", "easily", "unleash", "supercharge".
- Prefer a full stop or a comma to an em dash.
- State defaults, ranges and limits as numbers. Say what happens at the edges, because that is
  what a reader comes to a reference for.
- No filler sections. A page with nothing to say under a heading doesn't have that heading.

## Page shape

```mdx
---
title: Markers
description: One sentence, what this page helps you do. Search results show it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

What the feature is for, in a sentence or two.

<AtAGlance menu="Mark ▸ Add Marker" keys="M" tools="add_marker" />

<Shot name="04-editor.window" alt="What the picture shows, for someone who can't see it." />

## Add a marker

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the moment.
2. Press <kbd>M</kbd>.

</Steps>

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |

## Good to know

Limits, edge cases and what stops it, in plain words.

## Related

- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
```

Every section is optional except the opening. Order the task sections as a reader needs them.

- **Headings** start at `##`, are sentence case, and name the job: "Add a marker", not "Adding".
  A feature in `src/data/features.json` with an `anchor` needs a heading that makes that anchor.
- **Menus** are bold with `▸`, spelled as the app spells them: **Clip ▸ Split**.
- **Keys** use the app's symbols in `<kbd>`: <kbd>⌘T</kbd>. Inside `AtAGlance`, pass the string.
- **Controls** are bold where they appear in a step: choose **Save**.
- **Links** are root-absolute with a trailing slash: `/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker`. The build
  fails on a link or anchor that does not exist.
- **Asides** are for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration: `:::note`, `:::tip`,
  `:::caution`, `:::danger`.
- **Screens** come from `src/assets/screens/`. A `name` is the file name without its look and
  extension. Use a screen only when it shows what the page is about, not when the thing is out
  of frame, and give it real alt text.

## MDX traps

MDX is JSX. In prose, `{`, `}` and `<` start code. Put anything like `{x}`, `<1 s` or `a<b` in a
code span, or write it out ("under 1 s"). `<kbd>` and every component must close. A line starting
with `import` or `export` is code. Leave a blank line after an opening component tag and before
its closing tag, or the Markdown inside won't render.

## Checking a page

```sh
node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs <page.mdx>…        # parses, imports, links, captures
python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages <page.mdx>…  # internal words, local paths
pnpm build                                                # in docs/site: the last word
```

## Screens

The captures come from the screen catalog (`designs/screens/`, `tools/proof/screens.py`), so the
pictures are of the real app. To refresh them:

```sh
python3 tools/proof/screens.py --out <dir>                      # from the repository root
node docs/site/scripts/import-screens.mjs <dir> --used
```

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, or a
page that names something internal.

---
title: Motion presets
description: Give a clip a ready-made entrance, exit or continuous movement that's tied to its two ends and stays with it through a trim.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A motion preset says what a clip does rather than where it is: how it arrives, how it leaves and what it does in between. It's tied to the clip's two ends, so it goes with the clip through a trim and there's nothing to reposition afterwards.

Each clip has three slots, and all three can run on the same clip:

- **In** is an entrance at the clip's start. See [Entrance and exit presets](/motion/entrances-and-exits/).
- **Out** is an exit at the clip's end, from the same nine kinds.
- **During** is a movement for the clip's whole length. See [During presets](/motion/during-presets/).

Presets work on any clip that draws a picture: video, still images, text, shapes, graphics and nests.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Clip ▸ Motion ▸ In', 'Clip ▸ Motion ▸ Out', 'Clip ▸ Motion ▸ During', 'Clip ▸ Motion ▸ Preview']}
  where="Clip tab ▸ Clip sub-tab ▸ Motion presets"
  tools="set_video"
/>

## Give a clip a preset

<Steps>

1. Select the clip.

2. In the Clip tab, pick the **Clip** sub-tab and open **Motion presets**, the last section. It's closed until you open it.

3. Choose a kind from **In**, **Out** or **During**.

4. Set **In Duration** or **Out Duration**, or for a During movement, **Amount** and **Period**.

5. Choose **Preview** to watch it loop.

</Steps>

If the defaults suit you, [the Motion menu](#use-the-motion-menu) is quicker.

## The Motion presets section

| Row | What it does | Range | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **In** | How the clip enters. | None and nine kinds | None |
| **In Duration** | How long the entrance takes. Dimmed while **In** is None. | 0.1 to 10 s, with quick picks of 0.25, 0.5 and 1 | 0.5 s |
| **Out** | How the clip leaves. | None and nine kinds | None |
| **Out Duration** | How long the exit takes. Dimmed while **Out** is None. | 0.1 to 10 s, with quick picks of 0.25, 0.5 and 1 | 0.5 s |
| **During** | What the clip does for its whole length. | None and five kinds | None |
| **Amount** | How strong the During movement is. Dimmed while **During** is None. | 0 to 100%, with quick picks of 25, 50, 75 and 100 | 50% |
| **Period** | How long one cycle of the During movement takes. Dimmed while **During** is None, and for Drift, which has no cycle. | 0.1 to 10 s, with quick picks of 0.25, 0.5, 1 and 2 | 1 s |
| **Preview** | Loops the clip so you can [watch its motion](#preview-a-preset). | | |

The two durations and **Period** snap to the project's frame grid. The In is measured from the clip's first frame and the Out back from its last.

With the section closed, its header sums up the clip's presets, for example "in fade · out slide left · pulse". With no presets it reads "off".

## Use the Motion menu

**Clip ▸ Motion** has three submenus, **In**, **Out** and **During**. Each lists its kinds, then **None** to clear the slot. They work on every selected clip that has a picture, and they're dimmed when no selected clip has one. None of them has a keyboard shortcut.

A checkmark shows the kind every selected clip shares. If the clips disagree, nothing is checked. If none of them has a preset in that slot, **None** is checked.

## Change or clear a preset

Choosing a different kind keeps the settings the slot already had: an In or Out keeps its duration, and a During keeps its amount and period. A slot you fill for the first time starts at the defaults, 0.5 s for an In or Out, and 50% with a 1 s period for a During.

To clear one slot, choose **None**. To clear all three, choose **Reset** in the section's header. **Reset** shows only when the clip has a preset to clear, and it clears every selected clip.

Each change is one undo step, however many clips are selected.

## Set presets on several clips

With several clips selected, a change to one slot leaves each clip's other slots as they were. Choosing a new In kind doesn't touch anyone's Out, and each clip keeps its own In duration.

The section shows the first selected clip's values, with **mixed** beside a row where the clips differ. That has two effects to watch for:

- **In Duration**, **Out Duration**, **Amount** and **Period** only change the clips that have a preset in that slot. The others are left alone.
- Those rows are dimmed by the first clip alone. If the first selected clip has no In, **In Duration** is dimmed even when other selected clips have one.

## Preview a preset

Choose **Preview** in the section, or **Clip ▸ Motion ▸ Preview**. Frame Job sets the [in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/) to the clip, turns [Loop](/timeline/loop/) on, moves the playhead to the clip's start and plays.

With several clips selected, it loops the first selected clip that has a picture.

The range and Loop stay until you clear them. Choose **Mark ▸ Clear Range** (<kbd>⌥X</kbd>) and click the **Loop** button in the toolbar. A range you'd already set is replaced.

## Read presets on the timeline

Small marks on a clip's name strip show its presets:

- **A wedge at each end** along the bottom of the strip stands for an In or an Out. It's as long as the preset's duration at the current zoom, and at least 2 points wide so a short preset still shows. The Clip tab's [action lane](/motion/action-lane/) shows the same two wedges.
- **A wave symbol** at the right end of the strip stands for a During movement. On a clip too narrow to fit it, the symbol is left out.

See [Reading a clip on the timeline](/timeline/reading-a-clip/) for everything else a clip draws.

## Motion sits on top of placement

A preset works relative to the clip. Frame Job takes the clip's own placement and any [actions](/motion/actions/) first, then applies the preset on top:

- Its scale and opacity multiply the clip's own. A clip at 50% opacity fades in to 50%, not 100%.
- Its rotation and offset add to the clip's own.
- Anything that changes the clip's size or turns it does so about the clip's visible centre, after any crop.
- The drawn size stays within the 1% to 1,000% that **Scale** allows.

The three slots add up the same way, so a clip can slide in while it pulses.

### The inspector shows un-moved values

The fields in the Clip tab show the clip's own numbers, even while the preview and the export show it moving. Halfway through a Zoom In, **Scale** still reads what you typed. That's why editing a clip's position or size works the same with a preset on it.

### Dragging during motion

A drag on the canvas changes the clip's own position, starting from where it sits without the preset. If you drag partway through a preset, the distance you drag is added to that un-moved position, and the preset keeps playing on top of it. To place a clip by eye, park the playhead where its In has finished and its Out hasn't started.

## Overlong presets shorten

When an In and an Out together last longer than the clip, Frame Job doesn't refuse them. It shortens both in proportion to their lengths, so the entrance ends on the frame where the exit begins. A 2 s In and a 1 s Out on a 1.5 s clip play as 1 s and 0.5 s. An In or Out alone that's longer than the clip plays over the clip's whole length.

On the timeline the wedges keep their full length, so they overlap. That's how to spot it. **In Duration** and **Out Duration** keep what you set too, so if you lengthen the clip later, the presets get their full time back.

## Inactive presets

An In or Out with a zero duration can come from an agent or an older project. Frame Job keeps it but it does nothing, and it draws no wedge. It's marked so you can fix it:

- The section's summary reads, for example, "in fade (inactive)".
- The **Clip ▸ Motion** submenus read **Fade (inactive)**, or **Fade (some inactive)** when only some of the selected clips with that kind have a zero duration.
- A note at the top of the section reads "Selection includes inactive In motion (zero duration). Increase Duration to reactivate; choose None to clear." It names **In**, **Out** or **In and Out**, and it counts every selected clip.

Changing the kind doesn't fix it, because a new kind keeps the old duration. Raise **In Duration** or **Out Duration**, or choose **None**.

## Presets and actions

An [action](/motion/actions/) animates a property to a value you set, over a span you place on the clip. A preset is anchored to the clip's ends and says what the clip does. Use a preset for an entrance, an exit or a repeating movement, and an action when a value has to reach a particular number at a particular moment.

A preset is never part of an action, and no action can animate one. While an action is selected, the section's rows are marked ⊘ and the section reads "Actions don't animate this. Edits here change the clip." Your edits there write the clip, as they do with no action selected, and **Reset** is still available.

## How edits treat a preset

| Edit | What happens to the presets |
| --- | --- |
| Trim | Each preset moves with its edge and keeps its length. |
| [Split](/editing/splitting/) | The first half keeps the In and gives up the Out, and the second half keeps the Out and gives up the In, so the cut doesn't play an exit and an entrance. Both halves keep the During. |
| [Change the speed](/speed/change-speed/) | The presets aren't rescaled. A 0.5 s In stays 0.5 s, and a clip that gets much shorter can make its presets [shorten](#overlong-presets-shorten). |
| [Freeze frame](/speed/freeze-frame/) | The still has no preset, and it sits at the clip's un-moved position, so a freeze taken mid-motion can jump. |
| [Add Blurred Background](/canvas/blurred-background/) | The backdrop copy doesn't move. The clip in front keeps its presets. |
| [Duplicate](/editing/duplicate-clips/), [Detach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/) and [Paste](/editing/copy-and-paste/) | The presets are kept. |
| [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/) | Presets are copied with the rest of the picture settings. |

A During movement restarts at each cut, because each piece is a clip of its own. [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) on a clip with Pulse or Drift can make it jump at the cuts.

## Good to know

- A preset moves the picture only. A Fade leaves the sound as it is, so use [audio fades](/audio/fades/) for that.
- A preset on a [nest](/editing/nests/) moves everything inside the nest together.
- [Adjustment clips](/color/adjustment-clips/) have the section and draw the marks, but a preset on one does nothing.
- [Motion blur](/motion/motion-blur/) blurs a preset's movement like any other.
- [Zoom to Region](/motion/zoom-to-region/) works out its zoom without a During movement, and tells you so with "This clip has During motion — the zoom is solved without it".
- [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/) works on an upright picture, so it won't take a clip with Spin in any slot.
- Changing the project's frame rate moves the durations and the period onto the new frame grid.

## With an agent

An agent sets and clears presets with `set_video`. It can change one slot and leave the others alone, or clear all three at once.

An agent isn't held to the section's ranges. Any duration of zero or more is accepted, which is how an [inactive preset](#inactive-presets) comes about, and a period can be outside 0.1 to 10 s as long as it isn't zero. An amount outside 0 to 100% is refused.

`get_project` answers the clip's un-moved values, so use `render_frame` to see a preset's effect. `set_action_end` won't take a preset, not even to clear one. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/).

## Related

- [Entrance and exit presets](/motion/entrances-and-exits/)
- [During presets](/motion/during-presets/)
- [Actions](/motion/actions/)
- [Transitions](/motion/transitions/)
- [The Clip menu](/reference/clip-menu/)

title: Entrance and exit presets
description: What each of the nine In and Out presets does, from Fade to Pop, and how a slide works out where to start and stop.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

The same nine kinds fill a clip's **In** and **Out** slots. This page says what each one does at each end. To set one, see [Motion presets](/motion/motion-presets/).

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Clip ▸ Motion ▸ In', 'Clip ▸ Motion ▸ Out']}
  where="Clip tab ▸ Clip sub-tab ▸ Motion presets"
  tools="set_video"
/>

## How In and Out relate

An exit is the entrance played the other way. An In starts quickly and slows as the clip arrives. An Out starts slowly and speeds up as the clip leaves. Pop is the exception, because it has a spring of its own.

Sizes here are relative to the clip's own size, and fades to its own opacity. A clip placed at 50% scale that zooms in from 60% starts at 30%. See [Motion sits on top of placement](/motion/motion-presets/#motion-sits-on-top-of-placement).

## Fade

The clip's opacity changes and nothing else does.

- **As an In:** fades in from fully transparent.
- **As an Out:** fades out.

## Zoom In

The clip grows, whichever end it's at.

- **As an In:** grows from 60% to full size while fading in.
- **As an Out:** grows to 140% while fading out.

## Zoom Out

The clip shrinks, whichever end it's at.

- **As an In:** shrinks from 140% to full size while fading in.
- **As an Out:** shrinks to 60% while fading out.

## Slide Left

A slide names the direction the clip travels. It doesn't fade, so the clip stays at full opacity the whole way. This one travels left.

- **As an In:** slides in from the right edge.
- **As an Out:** slides out past the left edge.

## Slide Right

- **As an In:** slides in from the left edge.
- **As an Out:** slides out past the right edge.

## Slide Up

- **As an In:** slides in from the bottom edge.
- **As an Out:** slides out past the top edge.

## Slide Down

- **As an In:** slides in from the top edge.
- **As an Out:** slides out past the bottom edge.

## Spin

The clip makes half a turn, clockwise at both ends.

- **As an In:** spins half a turn into place, growing from 30% size and fading in.
- **As an Out:** spins half a turn away, shrinking to 30% size and fading out.

## Pop

The clip springs past full size, so this is the one to use when you want a bounce.

- **As an In:** grows from nothing, overshoots to about 110% and settles at full size. It fades in over the first quarter of its duration.
- **As an Out:** swells to about 110%, then shrinks to nothing. It fades out over the last quarter.

## How slides measure

A slide measures the clip as it's drawn, with its scale, rotation and crop, from wherever you've placed it. So it starts or ends exactly off the edge of the canvas, however large the clip is and wherever it sits.

Inside a [nest](/editing/nests/), that edge is the nest's own canvas rather than the project's.

## Slides on text

A text clip has no measured size, so a slide can't work out exactly where it leaves the canvas. It starts or ends half a canvas past the edge instead. That clears any text narrower than the canvas. Text wider than the canvas can still show at the start of a slide in or the end of a slide out.

## Good to know

- An Out's last frame still shows a sliver of the movement, because the exit finishes at the end of that frame. A Fade out isn't fully transparent on the clip's very last frame.
- Every kind works with every During movement, so a clip can slide in while it pulses. See [During presets](/motion/during-presets/).
- A preset only moves the picture. For sound, see [Audio fades](/audio/fades/).

## Related

- [Motion presets](/motion/motion-presets/)
- [During presets](/motion/during-presets/)
- [Transitions](/motion/transitions/)

The public user documentation: Astro with Starlight, one page per feature or tight family of

sidebar.mjs             every page's place in the navigation, in order
src/content/docs/       the pages: <section>/<page>.mdx

src/assets/screens/     WebP captures, written only by scripts/import-screens.mjs
src/styles/             the brand: the mark's inks, the app's faces, square chrome
```

refusal is checked against `app/Sources/`, `core/src/`, `graphic/` or `mcp-proxy/` before it is

probably does. If the code cannot settle it, leave it out.

`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.

Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.

So a page never mentions: spec or decision IDs (`AU-12`, `§11`), road maps, phases, issue numbers,
source file or type names, `rc_*` exports, format version numbers, proofs, tests, or the history

MCP pages and `tools=` in `AtAGlance` name agent tools, because those are the product's interface.

66	
67	The clip makes half a turn, clockwise at both ends.
68	
69	- **As an In:** spins half a turn into place, growing from 30% size and fading in.
70	- **As an Out:** spins half a turn away, shrinking to 30% size and fading out.
71	
72	## Pop
73	
74	The clip springs past full size, so it overshoots where the others stop.
75	
76	- **As an In:** grows from nothing, overshoots to about 110% and settles at full size. It fades in over the first quarter of its duration.
77	- **As an Out:** swells to about 110%, then shrinks to nothing. It fades out over the last quarter.
78	
79	## How slides measure
80	
81	A slide measures the clip as it's drawn, with its scale, rotation and crop, from wherever you've placed it. So it starts or ends exactly off the edge of the canvas, however large the clip is and wherever it sits.
82	
83	Inside a [nest](/editing/nests/), that edge is the nest's own canvas rather than the project's.
84	
85	## Slides on text
86	
87	A text clip has no measured size, so a slide can't work out exactly where it leaves the canvas. It starts or ends half a canvas past the edge instead. That clears any text narrower than the canvas. Text wider than the canvas can still show at the start of a slide in or the end of a slide out.
88	
89	## Good to know
90	
91	- An Out finishes at the end of the clip's last frame, not on it, so that frame still shows a sliver of the clip. A Fade isn't quite fully transparent there.
92	- Every kind works with every During movement, so a clip can slide in while it pulses. See [During presets](/motion/during-presets/).
93	- A preset only moves the picture. For sound, see [Audio fades](/audio/fades/).
94	
95	## Related

97	- [Motion presets](/motion/motion-presets/)
98	- [During presets](/motion/during-presets/)
